I have farmed this land in the North West for many years. The soil is sandy and tired, so I will buy one bag of inorganic fertilizer from the agro-dealer to give the millet some strength, but I cannot spend too much because money is tight. I also have cow manure that I will spread on the field before the rains come. I will plant with my own millet seed saved from last year's harvest — it grows well here and I know it. I have no money for chemicals or irrigation, so we will pull the weeds by hand and trust in the rains. My family will do the bulk of the work, but I may hire two or three young men for a few days when the harvest is heavy.
